label: run-summary
headline: A round's account is now an artefact a gate reads, an absence is a different verdict from a stub, and the mechanism was tested by killing three real writers -- but it makes a lost report recoverable and cannot make a report happen.

pre_registration: Nine falsifiers written to scratch before any file was created. F1 (a killed writer's record unreadable) did not fire: three real kills, all recovered as predicted. F2 (a rosterless design reports absence soundly) did not fire: absence stayed uncomputable without a roster, so the roster ships. F3 (the gate landable only at a flattering rank) did not fire: owed_forward plus a waiver took it at 37 of 39. F5 (mutation INERT or UNRESTORED) did not fire: DEMONSTRATED in two mirrors. F6 (docs-code drift silent) did not fire. F7 (a discriminator exists between died-before-filing and never-launched) did not fire, so the limit is stated rather than closed. TWO FIRED. F4 fired before the file was written and is recorded as such: I predicted no gate-mutation run newer than 34099756605 existed and was wrong -- run 34308556192 had demonstrated the two owed gates two days earlier and nobody had read it, which is D-106 again. F8 fired: the baseline was not green, because a concurrent workstream's in-flight edit had two tests red, and I destroyed that edit with git checkout before understanding it.
how_it_fails: It makes a lost report RECOVERABLE and does not make a report HAPPEN. An agent that dies before its penultimate tool call files nothing, and no gate here can tell that from an agent that was never launched; the roster narrows it to who was expected, and this round's roster was written by a workstream rather than the launcher, so it declares itself incomplete and its absences are a lower bound. Closing it needs the launcher to write a start record. Two smaller holes: a JSON summary is still self-assessment, cheaper to write and not more trustworthy, and .github/run-summaries/ is outside tools/check_claims.py's SCAN_GLOBS, so a number inside a summary is an unbacked claim nothing reddens.
not_done: No in-situ evidence for the new gate. It is owed forward; this workstream cannot push, so the run that lands the commit is the run that owes it.
The register holds one round with one workstream, so the committed data exercises `complete` and nothing else. The other five states are exercised only in tests and by the mutation.
SCAN_GLOBS was not extended to .github/run-summaries/, so numbers inside a summary are ungated. That file carries two ratchets this workstream does not own.
Nothing checks that a roster names every workstream actually launched. roster_complete is a self-report about a self-report.
Harvesting a gate-mutation run is still a person deciding to run `gh run view`. This round did it and installed nothing that makes the next round do it.

A concurrent workstream's uncommitted edit to tools/check_claims.py was destroyed by my `git checkout --` and restored from two hunks visible in my transcript. I cannot rule out that a third hunk existed.

claims_for_sampling: tools/run_summary.py refuses a summary carrying an unknown key, one whose claims_for_sampling is not exactly twelve entries, and one whose label disagrees with its filename stem.

The reader distinguishes six states -- complete, partial, vacuous, invalid, unreadable, absent -- and tests/test_run_summary.py::TestTheReader::test_every_state_is_reachable_and_distinct asserts all six against one directory in one call.
`absent` is computed against a roster declared in round.toml and is not computable from a directory listing, which is why a rosterless --report exits 2 while still printing every summary it found.
A child process killed with Popen.kill after an atomic write is read back as `complete`, and the prose file it would have written next does not exist on disk.
A child process killed part-way through a non-atomic write is read back as `unreadable`, and a roster label with no file at all is `absent` in the same report.
A child process killed inside write_summary with os.replace stalled leaves no file at the target path and a .tmp sibling in the round directory.
gates.run_summary is registered at cost_rank 37 of 39, and ruff and ruff_format moved from 37 and 38 to 38 and 39 with nothing else in the ordering changing.
python tools/gates.py --mutate run_summary returned `DEMONSTRATED  mutated rc=1, restored rc=0` in two separate mirrors of the working tree on 2026-09-09.
The new gate carries no in-situ evidence and IN_SITU_TRAJECTORY records it as one gate owed forward under a waiver, with the debt at 21 against a ceiling of 21.
figures and memo_identity came back DEMONSTRATED in GitHub Actions run 34308556192 at commit 4ef57c8, which is what raised the register's in-situ count from 16 of 38 to 18 of 39.
python tools/run_summary.py --check does not fail on a workstream that filed nothing or filed a stub that says nothing, and TestTheGate asserts both of those separately.

I destroyed a concurrent workstream's uncommitted edit to tools/check_claims.py with git checkout --, recovered two hunks verbatim from my own transcript and re-applied them, and cannot establish that no third hunk existed.
